question:
There is a unique two-digit positive integer $t$ for which the last two digits of $11\cdot t$ are $36$.

What is $t$?
solution:
The last two digits give $11t\equiv36\pmod{100}$. Since $11\cdot9=99\equiv-1\pmod{100}$, multiplying by 9 gives $-t\equiv324\equiv24\pmod{100}$. Hence $t\equiv-24\equiv76\pmod{100}$. The only two-digit integer in this residue class is 76.
Final answer: 76
